newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: COLSTON'S OFFICE SAYS HE WON'T RESIGN FROM SENATE
The office of Independent Senator Mal Colston says the Senator has no intention of quiting the Senate, despite expectation's he'll resign as Senate Deputy President later today.
The Queensland senator has so far resisted calls to stand down, while the Federal Police investigate allegations he rorted his travel claims.
Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot plans to move a motion of no confidence and another to declare the position vacant and choose a replacement when the Upper House sits today.
Senator Kernot says the Senator should no longer be in the Parliament.
It's expected Senator Colston will resign from Deputy President's job early this afternoon, just before the house sits, to avoid the moves against him.
The Opposition and Greens intend to push for an inquiry into whether Senator Colston misled the Senate.

FAIRFAX STAFF STRIKE AGAINST CHANGES TO CROSS-OWNERSHIP LAWS Fairfax supporters say the goal of today's strike is to convince the Federal Cabinet there will be terrible consequences if the number of Australia's media proprietors is reduced to two.
Fairfax Newspapers' staff will go on strike for six hours tomorrow to campaign against changes to cross-media ownership laws.

Friends of Fairfax spokesman Matthew Moore says they believe three proprietors is the absolute minimum Australia should have. As part of the strike, about 300 Sydney staff will be distributing leaflets to morning commuters, asking them to lobby Ministers to keep diversity in media ownership.
NSW BUDGET TO BE DELIVERED TODAY
The Carr government in New South Wales will hand down it's third budget today.
Premier Bob Carr says public transport, schools, police and hospitals will be safe from cuts.
But he there'll be a possible increase in the tax paid on unimproved land worth more than half-a-million dollars.
Mr Carr says while the diesel and petrol tax cuts won't be a good as those given to country Victoria last month, he's going easy on the bush.
And 70-million of the 23-billion dollar budget, will be put aside to pay for the tollways cashback scheme.
COLSTON SON IN CANBERRA MEDIA SCUFFLE
A Channel Ten cameraman was involved in a scuffle with one of Senator Mal Colston's sons tonight.
After Senator Colston flew into Canberra and eluded waiting media at the airport, television crews pursued Senator Colston by car, to his flat.
Senator Colston faces a no-confidence motion in the Senate tomorrow, if he doesn't resign as Senate Deputy President.
A Channel Ten spokesperson claims the cameraman was punched several times in the head and kicked.
The spokesperson says the cameraman is seeking medical attention for cuts to his face and a bloodied nose and is considering whether to lay charges.
CENTURY ZINC ARBITRATION DUE TO RECOMMENCE
Native Title Tribunal arbitration hearings will re-start in Mt Isa today after being adjourned for 24 hours yesterday at the request of Century Zinc.
The company, which is planning to develop a giant zinc mine in Queensland's Gulf country, said yesterday it was close to reaching agreement with all parties on the mine.
The company's lawyers told the sitting that if investigations began, it was likely goodwill established in recent discussions would diminish.
Century Zinc Managing Director, Ian Williams, says he'll discuss the agreement and clarify several matters to the six native title claimants present at yesterday's sitting.
Company Spokesman, Greg Walker, says Mr Williams may meet with the Queensland Premier and ATSIC Deputy Chair Ray Robinson later today to view the agreement governing the project's go ahead.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
